article.title: NFL EDGE Saturday Morning Brief
article.dek: Lamar is still a game-time call, the Value card moved to Las Vegas, and the overnight board mostly drifted rather than flipped.

items.headline: Lamar still a game-time call — no new overnight news
paragraphs: Nothing changed overnight on the weekend's biggest question. Lamar Jackson is still officially questionable for Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET game against the Bengals, still working through the high ankle sprain he confirmed Friday, still saying he's 'heading in the right direction' without committing. Tyler Huntley starts if he can't go.

The app's QB row still lists Lamar as questionable, and the line is steady at Bengals -1.5. This is the one game to wait on: the decision lands with inactives, about 90 minutes before kickoff. When it lands, Check your number — don't guess on a game-time ankle.
items.takeaway: One game waits for a real event: Lamar's call, about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff.

items.headline: Injury roundup: the designations that still stand
paragraphs: Baker Mayfield is expected to start at Carolina after missing three games with a dislocated right thumb, though the app's QB row still lists him questionable. The catch from Friday still holds: the Bucs ruled out receiver Emeka Egbuka, right tackle Luke Goedeke, and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. A returning starter behind a backup right tackle, without his top receiver.
San Francisco heads to Atlanta shorthanded: the 49ers ruled out receivers Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel plus pass rusher Nick Bosa. No new designations landed overnight for any other Sunday game.
items.takeaway: Mayfield's return is real, the supporting cast is thinner, and the 49ers are the weekend's biggest absence list.

items.headline: Weather: no games today, calm Sunday in Baltimore
paragraphs: There are no NFL games today, so there's no kickoff weather to check. For Sunday, the Baltimore forecast at the 1:00 p.m. ET window is sunny, high around 67, light wind. That's a fact, not a totals edge — nothing in it argues the total either way.
Final forecasts for Sunday's other outdoor windows come with the Sunday morning edition, closer to kickoff.
items.takeaway: Baltimore looks calm and clear Sunday; the rest of the outdoor slate gets its final check Sunday morning.

items.headline: Sunday starts early: 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff
paragraphs: The slate's first game kicks off before most of the country has had coffee: Steelers at Saints at 9:30 a.m. ET. The board has Pittsburgh -3 at both books and the total at 44.5.
That early window means the first inactive list of the day lands early too. Check that price Saturday, and again Sunday morning — it's the first decision of the day, not an afterthought.
items.takeaway: Early game, early decision: get the 9:30 a.m. ET price checked before Sunday morning gets busy.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Your three cards Saturday morning
paragraphs: Hit Rate: Vikings moneyline -290 (DraftKings), Colts at Vikings. The model's win probability is 78.6% — the most likely to win on the board. The evaluator EV is -0.028, and that's fine: Hit Rate forgoes value for win probability. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate ≠ Profit Rate, and that's the job description, not a flaw.
Balanced: Browns moneyline -130 (DraftKings), Browns at Titans. Model 71.9%, EV +0.013. The middle ground: a strong pick without paying too much, a good starting point for a new bettor.
Value: Raiders +3.5 -120 (FanDuel), Rams at Raiders. Always the model's +EV play, EV +0.005. It rotated off Saints +3 overnight — the card follows the price, not the team.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate = most likely to win. Balanced = strong without overpaying. Value = the +EV play. Check = the verdict on your price.

items.headline: Monday night: the model and the market still disagree
paragraphs: Cowboys at Eagles: the model's expected margin has this about a pick'em, while the market board has Dallas -4.5 at both books. Nothing changed overnight — the model didn't budge, and the price barely did.
Tanner McKee makes his second straight start for Philadelphia. When the model says pick'em and the market says -4.5, don't guess — run your number through Check. Monday game? Monday check.

items.headline: Learn the Game: handle vs. tickets
paragraphs: (Hypothetical example:) Imagine a sportsbook's split board shows 70% of the tickets on the favorite, but only 40% of the money. Tickets count bets; handle counts dollars. When the two disagree, it means a smaller number of bigger bets is on the other side — that's the gap people mean when they talk about a public-vs-sharp split.

What could it mean? Not much on its own. A split is only interesting when it comes with something else — the line moving against the ticket-heavy side, or a second book showing the same shape. Tickets and handle agreeing on one side is not a disagreement at all.
How to apply it: don't chase a split you can't verify. If your book shows a split and the line is moving, type the current number into Check and let the app price what's left.
items.takeaway: Tickets count bets, handle counts dollars — a split only matters when the two disagree and the line backs it up.

items.headline: Overnight: ticks, not flips — and one card rotation
paragraphs: A quiet night after a loud Friday. No spread flipped sides. The Bengals -1.5 price ticked from +100 to -105 at DraftKings (Ravens +1.5 -120 to -115) on the same Lamar news — the market holding its position, not extending it.

Elsewhere it was small drift: Broncos -238 to -230, Vikings -298 to -290, Texans -520 to -500 at DraftKings, Steelers -166 to -162, Saints +3 -108 to -110. The Browns moneyline split the books — -135 to -130 at DraftKings, -126 to -132 at FanDuel — a reminder that your book's number is the only one that matters.
The one real change: the Value card rotated from Saints +3 to Raiders +3.5 -120 at FanDuel. Same job, new price.

One timing note, and only one: Ravens-Bengals waits for Lamar's game-time call. For everything else, if your book has a good number and Check says bet, bet now — waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too, and Sunday brings the late public rush on big-name teams.

And the standing reminder: when the board hasn't picked up a move, or your book isn't DraftKings or FanDuel, tap Check, type in your book's line and price — the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: A quiet overnight board: price ticks everywhere, one card rotation, and one game that genuinely waits.

items.headline: Saturday's job: Check Sunday's prices before the rush
paragraphs: The board refreshes every morning and evening, and Saturday is the calm before the Sunday rush. Run each Sunday price through Check now — type in your book's line and price and get a bet/no-bet verdict on the number you can actually play. Start with the 9:30 a.m. ET early game, since its window closes first.
One honest note: settlement is manual. The tracker only works if you're honest with yourself — log the losers too, not just the ones that hit.
items.takeaway: Check Saturday's numbers before Sunday's public money moves them — and log every result, win or lose.
